recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. The current source satisfies FHIR-28498, and adding another duplicate-notification paragraph would reintroduce redundancy already cleaned up by FHIR-43516.
issue_request: FHIR-28498 was a Published/Persuasive FHIR-I R5 change request asking the Subscription documentation to explicitly say duplicate notifications are possible and that client applications need to handle them.
initial_application: The Jira comment identifies dbeb5e6a7aa3cba0705a1c337c0eaf6174d32eb2 as the application commit. That bundled subscription commit added source/subscriptions.html wording that some notifications might not be delivered and some might be delivered multiple times, plus mitigation guidance through delivery-error detection.
additional_context: The cited Zulip thread says the framework does not require guaranteed delivery and does not prevent duplicate delivery. FHIR-I minutes on 2020-11-09 record FHIR-28498 as Persuasive by 13-0-0. Later FHIR-43516 cleanup intentionally removed a duplicate overview copy while preserving the warning in Scoping Responsibilities and is already audited on the combined branch. A later FHIR-47280 refactor preserved the same content with current formatting.
reconciliation: No source change was made. Current source/subscriptions.html remains in build scope and states that delivery is not guaranteed, that clients should know some notifications might be delivered multiple times, and that Detecting Delivery Errors describes mitigation.

related_jiras.note: Cleaned up duplicate delivery-limitation wording while preserving the duplicate-notification warning in Scoping Responsibilities; already represented on the combined branch by 5ef92051039db6bee2cec864fc6d3f044256bba8.
Broader Subscription narrative refactor that reformatted source/subscriptions.html and preserved the warning in the current line history.
